# Solar Eclipse Workbench PRODUCTION script - total solar eclipse of 12 August 2026
# Generated by scripts/generate_20260812_production.py - edit that, not this file.
#
# Bodies : Fuji Fujifilm X-T4   (Fuji SDK + relay trigger on the remote jack)
#          Canon EOS 800D   (gphoto2)
# Optics : two 80/480 mm refractors, fixed f/6.  Neither body can drive a
#          telescope's aperture, so the aperture column is informational.
# Filter : ND 5.0 solar film on both, for every partial-phase frame.
#
# Site   : Palencia, N Spain  42.0095 N, -4.5289 E, 740 m
# Type   : Total, magnitude 1.0119, totality 101 s
#
#   C1     17:33:56 UTC   sun  18.9 deg
#   C2     18:29:10 UTC   sun   8.7 deg
#   MAX    18:30:00 UTC   sun   8.6 deg
#   C3     18:30:51 UTC   sun   8.4 deg
#   C4     19:22:34 UTC   sun  -0.8 deg
#   sunset 19:22:53 UTC
#
# Sunset eclipse: totality is only 8.6 deg up and the sun sets 19 s after C4, so the
# last partials are shot into horizon haze.  A clear, low western horizon matters more
# here than anything else.
#
# Why the two bodies do not always use the same command
# -----------------------------------------------------
# The rigs are identical, so the exposures are identical and both use take_picture
# everywhere the behaviour is the same.  Three forced differences:
#   corona ladders  take_hdr ramps the shutter between frames on gphoto2, but on the
#                   Fuji SDK path it fires 2*stops+1 frames at ONE speed.  The X-T4
#                   uses take_bracket (wired to the SDK bracket_no_download) instead.
#   contact bursts  only the X-T4 has the relay, so it free-runs CH at ~15 fps.
#                   The 800D holds its shutter through take_burst at ~6 fps.
#   fastest speed   1/8000 on the X-T4, 1/4000 on the 800D.  Only the beads frames
#                   are quick enough to notice; the 800D's are capped and run ~2/3
#                   stop over, which RAW absorbs.
#
# Atmospheric dimming
# -------------------
# The sun falls from 18.9 deg at C1 to the horizon and airmass climbs from 3.1 to over
# 30, so every filtered frame was computed for the sun altitude at that exact instant:
#   - above 5 deg : Jubier tables, interpolated in sun altitude and site height
#   - below 5 deg : the tables break down, so the 5 deg value is extrapolated with a
#                   Kasten-Young airmass and 0.25 mag/airmass extinction.
# That coefficient is a guess (0.15 clear .. 0.40 hazy) and the error grows to several
# stops at the horizon, hence the wide brackets after C3+18m.  Comments carry the sun
# altitude and airmass X used for each frame.
#
# Partial-phase frames alternate between the bodies, so the pair samples the disc
# twice as often as either alone.
#
# The relay must be connected and registered before the run, or every relay_* line is
# skipped with a warning and the X-T4 loses both contact bursts.  Firing the remote
# jack while the SDK holds the session is still an untested combination - bench it.
